title: In 1726 a woman claimed to give birth to rabbits, and the king's surgeon believed her

cover.alt: Mary Toft, in a white cap, sits up in a cottage bed under a patchwork quilt with a sly half-smile, while rabbits sit on the floor and a surgeon in a wig and plum coat stares in shock.

body: In the autumn of 1726 **Mary Toft**, a poor woman from Godalming in Surrey, appeared to give birth to pieces of animals, most of them parts of rabbits. Her man-midwife, John Howard, believed her and wrote to important people. **Nathaniel St André**, surgeon-anatomist to King George I, came to see, delivered part of a rabbit himself and published a pamphlet in support. Others were less sure: the king's German surgeon, Cyriacus Ahlers, suspected fraud, and in London, where crowds came to see her, a porter told magistrates he had been paid to smuggle in a rabbit. Threatened with a painful operation by Sir Richard Manningham, Toft confessed on 7 December. She was jailed for four months and released without trial. The doctors who had vouched for her became a national joke, and Hogarth drew them in his print *Cunicularii*.

slides.alt: A low cottage bedroom with dark beams. Mary Toft, in a white cap, sits up in bed under a patchwork quilt. An old surgeon in a white wig holds up a rabbit in astonishment; another rabbit sits on the floor.
slides.caption: Godalming, 1726. Mary Toft is 'giving birth' to bits of animals. Her man-midwife, John Howard, believes it.

bubbles.text: As soon as the eleventh rabbit was taken away, up leapt the twelfth!
bubbles.speaker: John Howard

slides.alt: John Howard grins in front of a shelf of glass jars, each holding a rabbit, and holds up a letter.
slides.caption: He keeps each 'rabbit' in its own pot of spirits, in order of arrival, and writes to everyone important.

bubbles.text: The king will want to hear about this.
bubbles.speaker: John Howard

slides.alt: A dashing surgeon in a white wig, a plum coat and a lace jabot bursts into the bedroom with his arms flung wide. Mary lies calmly in bed; Howard follows him in.
slides.caption: 15 November. The king's surgeon-anatomist, Nathaniel St André, arrives. She is in labour with rabbit fifteen.

slides.alt: By the bed, St André points eagerly at a glass of water in which a scrap of rabbit lung floats. A gentleman in a blue coat stares, astonished.
slides.caption: He delivers a piece of rabbit himself, drops a scrap of its lung in water and watches it float. Convinced.

slides.alt: A Georgian London street. A crowd of gentlemen in wigs and tricorne hats and ladies in caps queues at a lit doorway, where St André welcomes them in.
slides.caption: 29 November: she is moved to Lacy's Bagnio in London. 'Every creature in town' comes to see and feel her.

bubbles.text: Do you think she'll do one while we're here?
bubbles.speaker: A visitor

slides.alt: Outside the bagnio, a porter in a tricorne hat stands with a rabbit's ears poking out of his coat, facing a stern gentleman who points at it.
slides.caption: 4 December. The bagnio's porter tells the magistrates that her sister-in-law paid him to smuggle in a rabbit.

bubbles.text: Her sister-in-law gave me money for this. Thought you should know.
bubbles.speaker: The porter

slides.alt: Mary Toft, sweating, cowers in bed as a stern elderly surgeon in black holds up a large saw.
slides.caption: 7 December. Sir Richard Manningham proposes a very painful operation to get to the bottom of it. She confesses.

bubbles.text: It won't hurt a bit. Well, it will hurt a lot.
bubbles.speaker: Sir Richard Manningham

bubbles.text: All right! I'll tell you everything!
bubbles.speaker: Mary Toft

slides.alt: On a London street, a crowd laughs at a satirical print pasted on the wall, showing three wigged doctors and a rabbit. St André stands among them, crestfallen.
slides.caption: She is jailed for four months and freed without trial. The doctors become a national joke, drawn by Hogarth.

slides.question: What finally broke the hoax?
options: A bribed porter and a threat of surgery
A rabbit refused to come out
slides.explanation: The bagnio's porter testified that he had been paid to smuggle in a rabbit, and when Sir Richard Manningham threatened a painful operation, Toft confessed.
